A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Connector framework. Their complete main text, equations, figures and appendices A–G support comparison, and the original supplementary material can be matched despite additions and renumbering.

before.justification: Sections 6 and Appendix G report original connectivity-recovery simulations, perturbation experiments and analyses of rat frontal-cortex recordings.

after.justification: The original empirical work is retained, with additional heavy-tailed simulations, transformer comparisons, sensitivity analyses and generated-neuron evaluations.

M1.justification: The flow-matching CNFs, ridge-regression conditional-mean estimate and Gaussian maximum-entropy conditional remain unchanged (Section 4, Algorithm 1). The separate lrRNN training prerequisite is clarified; the heavy-tailed experiments test the existing procedure without introducing a new method component.

E1.justification: Figure S7 adds Student-t and log-normal synthetic connectivity distributions to the bistable-attractor evaluations. The existing attractor tasks, context-dependent decision-making task and rat recording dataset remain; the additional analyses do not introduce another behavioral task or recorded population.

E2.justification: Appendix G.3 and Figures S9–S10 add an evaluated NDT-like transformer latent-variable model, with the observation mapping in Equation (45), to the connectivity-identifiability comparison with LINT-based inference. The earlier comparison methods remain.

E3.justification: Supplementary protocols add regularization values 10^-2 and 10^-6 around the retained 10^-4 experiment, perturbation comparisons using 900 grid points and 100-step trajectories, and generated-activity snapshots at one second. Existing training budgets and five-fold splits remain unchanged; these are additional evaluations, not replacements of the original settings.

E4.justification: Validation substantially expands through regularization sensitivity (S1–S3), heavy-tailed conditional-distribution mismatch checks (S7), transformer loading-identifiability analysis (S9–S10), quantitative silencing comparisons (Table S1), and sampled-neuron population checks (S12). Earlier initialization and clustering robustness analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Figure S12 introduces two-sample, two-sided Kolmogorov–Smirnov tests; existing five-fold mean and standard-deviation reporting remains. Appendix G.5 newly describes eight lrRNN fits as independent, but their configurations already appeared in v1, so an increased run count is not established.

E6.justification: Main-figure results are retained, but substantial results are added. Table S1 reports LINT versus Connector flow-field MSE of 0.0894 versus 0.0097 and trajectory R² of 0.695 versus 0.929. New findings include regularization-dependent failure, heavy-tailed conditional mismatch despite similar dynamics, transformer activity R² = 0.99 despite loading mismatch, and S12 p-values of 0.27 and 0.12. These are newly reported evaluations, not version-to-version performance gains.

T1.justification: Appendix A.3 adds a mean-field derivation for jointly Student-t connectivity, using Gaussian scale mixtures to derive activity and variance-weighted gain expressions with a stated requirement of degrees of freedom greater than one. The revision also explicitly assumes strictly increasing activations and a unique loss-minimizing activity solution reached by training. Earlier derivations remain.

C1.justification: The abstract narrows the claim of a maximally unbiased connectivity distribution to being maximally unbiased over unidentifiable components. The main contributions—identifiability analysis, Connector, connectivity dissimilarity and synthetic/rat validation—remain unchanged.

C2.justification: Substantive additions qualify convergence by regularization strength (G.1), interpret the Student-t gain term (A.3), justify the iid/mean-field regime (G.5), and explain limits involving time-invariant connectivity and generating only task-relevant activity (Section 7, G.4.4). Section 4 also explicitly bounds downstream inference by the quality of the initial lrRNN fit.

D1.justification: A new Software and Data section supplies a code-repository link. Appendix G.6 specifies an NVIDIA TITAN X Pascal and typical Connector fitting time below one hour, whereas v1 only identified NVIDIA GPUs. Figure S7 documents heavy-tailed data generation; existing CNF architecture and optimization details remain.

R1.justification: New citations support Student-t scale mixtures, population-level reasoning, transformer identifiability, balanced networks and time-varying connectivity, including Andrews and Mallows, Ye and Pandarinath, Vafa et al., Pellegrino et al. and Lu et al. The central positioning relative to low-rank RNN inference and mean-field theory is retained.

P1.justification: The abstract and framework exposition receive targeted edits, and new appendix subsections organize the additions. Software and Data and Impact Statement sections are added, with revised acknowledgements and conference information. The existing main narrative and section order remain largely unchanged.

P2.justification: The visual evidence substantially expands with regularization curves, heavy-tailed flow-field/connectivity panels, LINT/transformer pairplots, generated-activity histograms and Table S1. Original main graphics remain; original supplementary figures are retained under new numbering, with resizing, relocation and restyling of the decision-task figure.

improvement.justification: Quantitative perturbation checks, regularization sensitivity and clearer recovery assumptions make v2's evidence and applicability easier to assess. The heavy-tailed and generated-neuron analyses add useful validation while acknowledging conditional-distribution mismatch and task-relevant-only coverage. Code-access and runtime disclosures also help reproducibility. These strengthen the supporting evidence and documentation of an otherwise retained method and main empirical account.
